title: Buffer API: Access, Rate Limits and Errors in 2026
summary: Buffer API schedules posts to connected channels. You'll understand the access requirements, rate limits, and what causes common errors.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is the Buffer API free to use?


Whether it's free depends on your Buffer plan and on the access rules in Buffer's developer documentation, so confirm both there before you build.


Record which account owns the access token, because the plan that account is on is the plan your integration inherits.


### Can I read analytics through the Buffer API?


Don't plan on it. The API is a publishing interface for creating and managing posts in queues, not a reporting feed for social-media performance data. Check the current endpoint list in Buffer's docs for whatever read access exists today.


If you need engagement metrics, pull them from each network's own API or from Buffer's dashboard exports, and treat any analytics you do get from Buffer as a bonus, not a dependency.


### Does Buffer still accept new API applications?


Check the developer pages on Buffer's site on the day you start, because registration rules for new applications have changed over time and a past answer may be stale.


If registration is closed or limited, you'll find out in the first hour rather than after you have built a scheduler around it.


Write down who at your organisation holds the application registration. When that person leaves, the connection shouldn't leave with them.


### Can I post to Instagram or TikTok through the Buffer API?


Only to the extent that Buffer's docs list those channels as supported for API publishing. A network that Buffer supports in its web app isn't automatically available through the API, and each network brings its own content-type restrictions.


Read the supported-channel and post-type details in the docs, then test one real post per channel from a non-production account before promising the feature to anyone.
